feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: clear positioning, relevant scope, and solid public-sector experience. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with opportunities to sharpen impact and streamline structure.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and career progression at NACo strongly support leadership credibility.  
- Good use of scale and specificity: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools/platforms add impact.  
- Broad yet coherent skill set: strategy, governance, analytics, CMS, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are presented as a consistent leadership profile.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce redundancy: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to make the CV tighter and easier to scan.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more results tied to growth, efficiency, engagement, or cost savings would strengthen impact.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation and bullet formatting vary across sections; “English (Native)” and “French (A2/Learning)” would read more cleanly as “Native” and “A2 (learning).” No major misspellings or grammar issues found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct, outcome-oriented language like “leading” or “modernizing.”
- Add one concrete proof point from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page website” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Trim the list slightly to avoid sounding exhaustive; group related areas such as “web, analytics, and editorial systems.”
- Possible rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivers scalable digital platforms, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled search experiences” is more specific and better supported.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” is close to the subtitle and competencies; consider simplifying.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened, made slightly more distinctive, and aligned in style.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and trim filler: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multichannel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations”
- Change “website” to “web” for a more senior, enterprise-level tone.
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” to sound more specific and less generic.
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest value: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, multichannel leadership, advocacy, multimedia.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid adding tools/platform names here.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with multiple experience bullets, so keep it concise rather than expanding it.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening the phrasing and making the format more scannable will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and purpose.
- Use parallel, outcome-oriented phrasing: “Launched/Built/Developed…” and trim stacked descriptors.
- Clarify technical specificity where it adds value: “hybrid retrieval + vector search” is strong; “bill-level AI chat” could become “bill-specific AI chat.”
- Consider this cleaner version:  
  **Selected Recent Projects**  
  **AI Hybrid Search** — Built an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-specific AI chat to improve policy-content discovery.  
  **We Are Counties Microsite** — Developed a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources, and a scalable modular architecture.  
  **Organization Anniversary Campaign** — Produced a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display integrated with the main site.  
  **Advocacy Video Series** — Led an ongoing advocacy video series across planning, production, and distribution for web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI search, microsite development, and advocacy video work are already referenced in Work Experience; keep this section shorter and more project-focused than role-focused.
- “Built/Developed” repeats heavily across entries; vary verbs slightly for polish.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear relevance to your headline, but it reads as a service list rather than a results-driven position. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact themes and avoid repeating NACo-era governance/analytics language unless you can show new scope or outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client type: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal campaign delivery, content operations, and enterprise web improvement.”
- Combine overlapping bullets on systems/governance/operations: “Built digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia communications.”
- Make technical delivery more outcome-oriented: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Sharpen the AI bullet: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and user-facing discovery experience.” Add metrics if available: launch status, content volume, adoption, speed, or engagement gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, analytics, workflows” overlaps with Director of Digital Media; keep this item focused on consulting impact and new builds.
- “Campaign microsites” and “AI search” already appear in Recent Projects; don’t repeat identical phrasing.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It can be sharper by foregrounding the biggest outcomes, tightening the opening, and avoiding overlap with earlier NACo roles on newsletters, video, and general digital operations.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with a tighter scope-and-impact line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website transformation and keep the metrics: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership outcome-focused: add growth, engagement, open rates, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements if available; otherwise trim “tens of thousands/thousands.”
- Combine operations/analytics bullets for concision: “Built NACo’s analytics and governance infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving reporting, publishing standards, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Newsletter and recurring video language overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, and systems.
- “Strengthened digital operations” is vague and repeats themes from multiple NACo entries.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to the scope you owned at this level: executional leadership, channel operations, and editorial coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize operational ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground scale: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add clearer outcome language: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with stronger verbs: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes and standardized digital publishing workflows to improve coordination, consistency and turnaround times.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning…” and “improved…publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s “governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.”
- Video-program language also overlaps with both the Director role and Recent Projects; keep this version focused on launch/expansion, not enterprise build-out.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent roles. It should be tighter and more distinctive, emphasizing leadership scope rather than repeating generic digital/content phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive language:
- Enterprise digital strategy for mission-driven organizations
- Editorial governance and cross-team publishing systems
- Multi-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Public-sector advocacy communications and audience-centered content planning
- Consider combining “public-sector and advocacy messaging” with “audience-focused content planning” to save space and avoid vagueness.
- Use “audience-centered” instead of “audience-focused” for a more polished, modern phrasing.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable proof for experience bullets rather than skills sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” is already strongly evidenced in the NACo Director role; avoid overloading the skills section with the same wording.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and group tools more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences
- Drop “WordPress” here unless it is important for target roles; Drupal is far more supported by recent experience.
- Remove “jQuery” from this topline section; it feels dated and is better kept only in Technical + IT if needed.
- Lead with outcomes-oriented capability labels rather than platform names alone, e.g., “CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and more strategic, with the detailed tool inventory below.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies, so avoid repeating identical phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI

- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize decision-making impact, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a tool list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity) • KPI framework design • Executive reporting • SEO and digital performance analysis”
- Put the highest-value capability first: lead with “Analytics infrastructure” or “Measurement strategy” rather than GA4.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Decision-ready reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier tied to recent work, such as “for enterprise web performance and content decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the full tool stack elsewhere; use this section for strategic framing and keep Technical + IT as the detailed inventory.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to studio buildout and event delivery rather than generic production terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more specific, senior phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Drop “video production and editing” if editing is already implied by multimedia tools; “broadcast-quality” better reflects the Director-level studio work.
- Consider adding scale or context if format allows: “Livestream and hybrid event delivery for advocacy, conferences and recurring programs”

- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies.
- “Livestream studio workflows” and podcast/video tools are already covered in Technical + IT, so avoid tool-level repetition here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest/recent platforms first: “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers tied to actual use: “Drupal (migration, microsites, governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful project; it feels less central than the other platforms.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; avoid listing platforms here and again elsewhere without added context.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already includes Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- If both sections remain, use Topline Skills for strategic capability and this section for tools with qualifiers only.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should emphasize implementation tools most relevant to recent work and use cleaner, more current phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Replace with: HTML/CSS • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) and consider removing jQuery unless it is still actively used in current freelance/Drupal work.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere in the CV, e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, automation, and lightweight serverless workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations.” Consider trimming one section or making this one more tools-focused.
- “GitHub Actions” may fit better under “Automation & Workflow Systems” if you want this item strictly front-end/dev oriented.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Workflow automation / Airtable systems” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize actual automation platforms over general collaboration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Project Systems
- Reorder by relevance/strength: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp
- If accurate, add light qualifiers instead of a pure list: Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate, Zapier (process automation) • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp (project/work management) • Slack, Microsoft Teams (team coordination)
- If space is tight, cut the lowest-signal tools first: Basecamp, Slack, Teams

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools and may dilute the stronger automation signal unless they were central to systems design.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Since the CV already shows strong email leadership in recent NACo roles, this item should signal enterprise-scale email/engagement capability rather than just naming tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, member communications)**
- If accurate, strengthen with scope: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • managed newsletter and member-email operations reaching tens of thousands**
- Keep the most relevant/current platform first; if Dynamics 365 is the strongest recent system, leave as-is, otherwise reorder by depth of use.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about newsletters reaching tens of thousands; don’t repeat the same metric here unless you remove it elsewhere.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid adding broad wording like “campaign management” unless it is platform-specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to show depth beyond platform names. Tightening the phrasing and making it more capability-led would reduce repetition.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO/performance analysis • KPI reporting • A/B testing
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI reporting” or “Executive reporting” for a stronger, more outcome-oriented capability.
- Order by strongest/recently evidenced tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this stack to impact in experience bullets rather than adding more tools here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This is nearly duplicated by “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider keeping the detailed tool list in only one place.
- “SEO” and “A/B testing” are broader capabilities, not tools; if you keep them here, pair them with similarly framed capabilities rather than pure platforms.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and the website refresh.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and contribution, e.g.: “Promoted across two digital roles as part of NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add clearer outcomes if available: website traffic growth, livestream/event volume, video cadence, email production volume, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence to concrete responsibilities: “Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped standardize day-to-day digital publishing workflows.”
- Replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with stronger phrasing if accurate: “mentored” or “supervised” a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the format rather than expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats language used in later NACo roles; specify early process-building instead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Add a second sentence focused on the standout media contribution: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a more specific verb, e.g., “produced supporting digital and multimedia content for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or output: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of research/projects coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad “digital content production” language that repeats later roles in digital media, video, and communications leadership.
- Don’t overstate team leadership or platform ownership here; those are better established in the 2015–2024 NACo roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so tighten it to tool proficiency only.

Suggested edit
